title: Eating when the power is out
summary: No-cook meals, what to eat first, and how to save fuel for the jobs that need a flame.

sources.title: FDA: Food and Water Safety During Power Outages and Floods
CDC: Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency
CDC: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency

blocks.text: Most stored food can be eaten with no cooking. **Canned food can be eaten straight from the can.** Save your stove fuel for boiling water.
This order follows the hold times: the fridge warms first, the freezer lasts longer, and the pantry lasts the longest.

items: **Fridge first.** It stays cold about 4 hours unopened. Eat or cook the most perishable food first (leftovers, meat, eggs, milk).
**Freezer next.** A full freezer holds about 48 hours, half-full about 24 hours. Eat what thaws first. Only refreeze food that still has ice crystals.
**Pantry last.** Canned and dry foods keep. Save them for when the rest is gone.

blocks.text: No-cook foods to keep on hand

items: Canned meats, fruits, vegetables and juices
Protein or fruit bars, dry cereal, granola
High-energy and comfort foods your household really eats
Infant food if you need it
A **manual can opener** and eating utensils

blocks.text: Choose foods your household will eat and plan for special diets. For a person with type 1 diabetes, see the T1D go-kit guide for what else to keep on hand.

items: Cook thawed or cold meat, poultry, fish and eggs **thoroughly**, to the safe minimum internal temperature on the package or a cooking chart. Cooking does not make spoiled food safe.
Use safe water (bottled or boiled) for cooking and mixing formula. FDA says ready-to-feed canned formula is the best choice when you can get it.
**Charcoal grills and camp stoves are for outdoors only.** Never cook indoors with them, in a garage, or in a tent.
Don't heat your home with a gas oven or stovetop.

blocks.text: Never use a grill, camp stove, or generator inside, even with doors open. See the carbon monoxide guide.
Fuel saver: use no-cook foods for most meals and keep your stove fuel for boiling water. The sources checked for this guide had no other fuel-saving numbers, so none are listed.
